Diagnose whether the Tweedie series-truncation M is adequate

Source: R/families.R
check_tweedie_truncation.Rd

Computes the per-observation Poisson rate lambda = mu^(2 - theta) / ((2 - theta) * phi) at the posterior mean of (mu, mphi, mtheta) and compares it against the truncation count M saved in the fit's standata. Warns if max(lambda) exceeds 0.7 * M, the rough point at which the log_sum_exp over m = 1..M starts to omit appreciable Poisson tail mass and bias the log-density downward.

Usage

check_tweedie_truncation(object, resp = NULL)

Arguments

object

An mvgam fit with at least one response whose family is tweedie().

resp

Optional name of one response to check. Without it, every tweedie() response is checked.

Value

Invisible NULL. Emits a message on the adequacy of M. It also emits a warning if M looks tight.

Details

The rate is taken for every response whose family is tweedie(). A multivariate model can name it for one response among several. All of them share the one M. mphi and mtheta are taken per observation. This covers a parameter given a formula of its own as well as a scalar one.

See also

tweedie() for the family and its argument M.

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(3)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = tweedie(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
             data = simdat$data_train, family = tweedie(),
             chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 32 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The largest Poisson rate the fit implies, against the default M = 30
check_tweedie_truncation(mod)
#> Tweedie truncation diagnostic. M = 30, max(lambda) at posterior mean = 4.97 (ratio = 0.166).

# A warning here would call for a refit with a longer series, such
# as family = tweedie(M = 60)
# }
